# An @mount that awaits is emitted inside a function marked async, and the
# settle chain above it starts it without waiting for it (ir.Call.Detached).
#
# The handler body is lifted into __effectN_mount, which __effectN_up calls,
# which the group settle calls. The checker coloured the program before any of
# those existed, so the mount was emitted as a plain `function` while its body
# wrote `await`. A settle that waited on the mount instead would hold every
# other bracket until the request answered. esbuild is what checks the bundle
# parses: this is a generate test rather than a golden for that reason.

sngl generate --out out app.sngl
exists out/index.html
grep 'async function __effect0_mount' out/index.html
! grep 'async function __effect0_up' out/index.html
! grep 'async function __effects0_settle' out/index.html

-- app.sngl --
import . "sngl:ui"
import api "js:./api"

output { none { html } }

component main node {
    var url = "a"
    var greeting = ""
    effect(on=url, @mount(k) {
        greeting = api.fetchHello(k)
    })
    text(value=greeting)
}

window {
    main
}
-- api/index.ts --
export async function fetchHello(name: string): Promise<string> { return "hi " + name; }
